title: Tool Capability Mediation

baseline.description: Green H checkpoint, tool calling refused outright. Not rewritten.

contractSpike.condition: IntentSmith must generate permission:{edit,write,bash,webfetch:"ask"}; under OpenCode defaults zero permission requests are emitted.

approvalGuarantees: Scoped to run + action + normalized payload hash.
Single consumption; approved and consumed are separate states.
TTL evaluated against the clock, not against whether a sweep ran.
Revoked on cancel, timeout, failure and restart recovery.
A pending approval found after a restart expires unanswered; a restart is not consent.
No allow-always exists and none can be expressed through the API.
The adapter never selects allow_always, whatever order the agent offers.
Append-only audit: requested, granted, denied, expired, revoked, consumed, mismatch.
Races settled by compare-and-set plus a per-approval mutex; the loser is told it lost.

verdicts.localInference: PROVEN. All inference goes through the authorized loopback gateway to local Ollama.
verdicts.strictOffline: NOT PROVEN. OpenCode fetches its provider catalog. No cloud traffic observed is not cloud traffic impossible.
verdicts.modelDefaults: NOT FIXED. The ten-formulation robustness run supersedes the repeated-prompt scores.

residualRisks: Cancel/timeout/process failure while a permission is outstanding is unproven against the real binary.
Parallel tool calls are refused, not supported.
skill, task, todowrite and webfetch payload shapes remain unobserved.
Mediation depends on the permission config IntentSmith writes; if it is absent or overridden the worker acts unmediated.
The residency HTTP 500 has a structural conclusion but no preserved wire sample.
qwen3.5:27b failed 2 of 10 path_escape formulations, which is the security-shaped case.
